session_note: Utah's 2026 General Session convened Tuesday, January 20, 2026 (the third Tuesday of January, per Utah Const. art. VI, sec. 2, which fixes a 45-day annual general session) and adjourned sine die on Friday, March 6, 2026. This is confirmed directly from le.utah.gov bill-action timestamps rather than assumed: HB0076's first House reading is logged 2026-01-20, and the three bills that did not pass (SB0231, SB0282, SB0318) were each formally struck (enacting clause removed) and 'Senate/ filed' as not-passed at 2026-03-06 23:59:55-23:59:59; HB0507's conference-committee resolution and final chamber sign-offs ran until 2026-03-06 20:49 (Senate) and 2026-03-07 00:16 (House, i.e. just after the midnight close of the 45th day). Utah bills do not carry over from one annual session to the next -- each general session (tracked internally by the Legislature as a distinct sessionID, e.g. '2026GS', '2025GS', '2020GS') is a discrete vehicle for bills, and a bill not passed and signed by sine die is dead for that year and must be reintroduced under a new bill number in a later session; this is illustrated directly by the packet itself, where the same general subject areas (data centers, large-load electric service) recur across separately numbered 2020, 2025, and 2026 bills.
